scope.summary: This standard prescribes the technical specifications, standard box styles, dimensional tolerances, and mechanical strength requirements (including bursting strength, puncture resistance, water absorbency, and top-to-bottom compression strength) for corrugated fibreboard boxes utilized in the packing, storage, and transportation of various commercial and industrial goods.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification / Packaging Code (Chemical Department / Paper and Paper Products)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a license to use the prestigious BIS 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) to print on box flaps as a certified assurance of quality, strength, and transit durability. Additionally, compliance with IS 13228 is strictly integrated into commercial export agreements, government food procurement tenders, and logistics standards across India.

requirements.detail: The outer liner of the corrugated box must undergo a 30-minute water absorption test (Cobb sizing test) conforming to IS 4006 (Part 1). The Cobb value (expressed in g/m²) must remain strictly within specified limits to ensure moisture-resistance during humid transit.

The finished board or liner must withstand a minimum bursting strength (expressed in kg/cm²) relative to its load capacity. For heavy-duty boxes (e.g., frozen seafood up to 25 kg), the bursting strength is capped at a minimum of 14 kg/cm².

For multi-ply corrugated boards (such as 5-ply or 7-ply constructions), a puncture resistance test (conforming to IS 4006 Part 1) must be conducted. For heavy-duty seafood shipments, the puncture resistance must be not less than 80 kgf·cm to ensure resistance to external impacts.

The completed, closed box must undergo top-to-bottom compression strength tests to verify stacking capacity. For high-weight seafood storage, the box must withstand a compression load of not less than 200 kgf/cm of base perimeter to prevent stack collapse.
Boxes must be manufactured in standard styles (such as Style 0201 regular slotted containers, or Style 0204 telescope containers) conforming to Indian guidelines and international FEFCO codes.

The manufacturer must ensure that the starch-based or silicate adhesives provide a uniform bond across all flutes without delamination. The manufacturer's joint (stitched or glued) must be secure, presenting no gaps or loose staples.

Any observed or calculated test or analytical value (such as bursting strength, compression load, or Cobb absorption) must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match the specified limit in this standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 13228 : 2006 (First Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard specification establishing technical requirements, mechanical properties, box styles, and testing methods for corrugated fibreboard boxes used in packing and transportation. Developed under the Paper and Paper Products Sectional Committee (CHD 15) and reaffirmed in 2022, this standard regulates corrugated boxes utilized across food, chemical, pharmaceutical, and logistics sectors. It unifies essential mechanical parameters—including water absorbency Cobb limits, bursting strength, puncture resistance, and top-to-bottom box compression—ensuring uniform box structural durability, moisture resistance in transit, and safe, stackable transport operations nationwide.
